newsitem.title: ITALY: Mercedes sees its Italian sales up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes sees its Italian sales up in 1997.

text.p: German vehicle maker Mercedes Benz, part of Daimler Benz AG, expects to see a rise in its own car volume sales in Italy by 26 percent to 47,000 vehicles in 1997, with overall sales up 21.9 percent to 3.445 trillion lire.
This was announced by the chairman of Mercedes Benz Italia Jochen Prange in a statement during a meeting with reporters.

Mercedes expects its 1997 quota of the Italian car market will rise to 2.5 percent from 2.1 percent of 1996. This will be helped by the launch in the autumn of 1997 of its new Class A car, that Mercedes hopes to sell around 2,300 units in the course of 1997 in Italy.
In 1996, Mercedes Italian car sales are expected to reach 37,138 vehicles, up some 8.1 percent on 1995.

In the industrial vehicle sector, Mecedes Benz Italy says this year it will hope to see a rise of 36.5 percent in a truck market set to fall 0.4 percent. Its quota of the market is set to a rise to 10.3 percent from 7.5 percent.
"Italy is confirmed as one of the principle world markets for Mercedes," Prango said in the statement.
